presentation.label: TAPE SATURATION
presentation.summary: JClones TapeHead on the DSP: a small tape-style saturator with drive, trim and three tone colours.
presentation.overview: TapeHead runs the input through a two-state recursion whose corner frequency COLOR sets, drives both states into cubic smoothstep curves and adds a clipped feedback term. Low DRIVE gives gentle rounding and a slight tilt; high DRIVE flattens peaks and thickens the low end. It is a buffer-free insert, so it runs on FX1 or FX2 of every track.
highlights: Port of JClones_TapeHead.jsfx, within 4.7e-4 of the float reference in a native render
DRIVE and TRIM as continuous 0-127 knobs over the JSFX ranges
COLOR: NORM, MED and BRGT corners at 2100, 3680 and 5000 Hz
No buffers: FX1 or FX2 on any track, 288 cycles/sample static
usage: Assign TAPEHEAD in FUNC + FX2 (or FX1) SETUP with LEVEL and YES. Defaults match the JSFX: DRIVE 36, TRIM 18 (-3 dB), COLOR NORM.

Use COLOR for brightness: MED and BRGT move the recursion's corner up and let more top end through the saturator.

controls.name: DRIVE
controls.doc: Tape drive. 0-127 maps to the JSFX drive 1-10 (gain 0.8x to 8x into the curves); 36 is about the JSFX default 3.5.

controls.name: TRIM
controls.doc: Output trim. 0 is 0 dB, 127 is -21 dB; 18 is the JSFX default -3 dB. Higher values are quieter.

controls.name: COLOR
controls.doc: Corner frequency of the recursion: NORM 2100 Hz, MED 3680 Hz, BRGT 5000 Hz.

limitations: The JSFX Clip switch is not exposed. Clip is always on (the JSFX default), because Q1.23 cannot carry the unclipped mode.

presentation.label: MODULATED SPACE
presentation.summary: A modulated feedback-delay reverb after the Erbe-Verb: size, decay past 100 %, absorb, chorus, grains, shimmer, reverse and tilt.
presentation.overview: Four delay lines with diffusing allpasses, absorbing low-passes and a soft-saturating decay feed each other through a Hadamard matrix at 22.05 kHz. DPTH sweeps from a cyclic chorus through random ergodic grains into octave shimmer; REV plays the pre-delay backwards; EDCY and ESIZ route the reverb's own envelope into decay and size. The dry signal is never processed.
highlights: Size from a 2 ms box to a 143 ms hall, gliding without zipper noise
Decay up to 120 %: sustains and saturates above about 106
Cyclic, ergodic and shimmer modulation on one bipolar knob, with its speed beside it
Reverse pre-delay, tilt EQ and envelope-to-decay/size routings
MIX 0 is the exact dry signal
usage: Choose E-Verb in FX2 SETUP: hold FUNC, press FX2, turn LEVEL to the end of the list and press YES.
On the main page, MIX (encoder F) sets dry/wet; SIZE, DCY and ABSB shape the space; DPTH left is chorus, right is grains, the last sixteen steps are shimmer; SPD sets how fast it moves.
On the SETUP page, TILT darkens or brightens the wet, PRE sets the pre-delay, REV reverses it, and EDCY/ESIZ send the reverb's envelope into DCY and SIZE.
The six main-page knobs take parameter locks, LFOs, scenes and MIDI CC like any stock effect's; the SETUP knobs are set per Part.

controls.name: SIZE
controls.doc: Scales every delay and allpass over six octaves: the longest line runs 2.2 ms at 0, 18 ms at 64 and 143 ms at 127. Moving it glides the pitch of the tail, smoothed per frame.

controls.name: DCY
controls.doc: Reflection gain from 0 to 120 %. Below about 106 the tail decays (short at 40, minutes at 100 with large sizes); above, it sustains and the in-loop saturation holds the level.

controls.name: ABSB
controls.doc: 0..38 adds diffusion (allpass gain up to 0.8); 38..127 adds damping inside the loop, darker and shorter.

controls.name: DPTH
controls.doc: Bipolar modulation, 0 at the centre. Left: cyclic chorus/doppler. Right: ergodic grains to +47; from +48 a growing share of grains glides up an octave (shimmer), about half at +56.

controls.name: SPD
controls.doc: Modulation speed 0.5 Hz to 256 Hz (about 12 Hz at 64): the cyclic rate or the grain rate; in the shimmer zone SIZE sets the grain length.

controls.name: MIX
controls.doc: Equal-power dry/wet. 0 is exactly the dry input; 127 is all reverb.

controls.name: TILT
controls.doc: SETUP A. Bipolar wet tone. Left: lows below 250 Hz up to +12 dB, highs down (about -14 dB at 9 kHz). Right: highs above 2 kHz up to +24 dB, lows down 3 to 5 dB. Centre is flat. Not lockable (SETUP page).

controls.name: PRE
controls.doc: SETUP B. Pre-delay 7 ms at 0, 42 ms at 64, 250 ms at 127; with REV on, the reverse window (at least 42 ms). Not lockable (SETUP page).

controls.name: REV
controls.doc: SETUP C. Plays the pre-delay buffer backwards in crossfaded windows; a change ducks, switches in silence and reopens without a click. Not lockable (SETUP page).

controls.name: EDCY
controls.doc: SETUP D. Bipolar: the reverb's envelope into DCY. Left reins the tail in when loud; right rings longer when loud, up to the decay of DCY 95, never into sustain (no effect from DCY 96 up). Centre is off. Not lockable (SETUP page).

controls.name: ESIZ
controls.doc: SETUP E. Bipolar: the reverb's envelope into SIZE. Left shrinks the space when loud; right grows it. Centre is off. Not lockable (SETUP page).

limitations: Owner reports working sound on MKII plus two distinct simultaneous T1/T5 instances, Part/project save and reload, and physical reboot on EVRB01T01. MKI, maximum-load silicon timing and broader hardware modulation/recovery tests remain unverified.
FX2 only: the effect needs the 16K-word delay buffer the OS gives FX2 instances.

With stock DSP code built in, E-Verb's 1,588 words take the space of two FX2-only stock reverbs. No tempo sync: as on the hardware and the stock reverbs, SPD is in Hz and PRE in milliseconds.

access.location: Audio track > FUNC+SRC > FM SYNTH; SRC for tone, LFO for voices/chords, FUNC+AMP for LEG.
steps: Open a disposable project with FM Synth firmware. Select an audio track, hold FUNC and press SRC, select FM SYNTH with UP/DOWN and press YES. No sample is required.
Press SRC. Set RATO to 1 and turn INDX from 0 upwards to hear a sine tone acquire FM harmonics. PTCH transposes it; FINE tunes it in cents; FDBK adds feedback; DEC shortens the modulation envelope.
Place a trig and press PLAY. Press LFO to set VOIC to 2–4 and CHRD to a chord if wanted. AMP ATK/HOLD/REL shape the gain envelope; FUNC+AMP exposes LEG.
Press STOP twice to silence the voice. To return to a sample machine, hold FUNC and press SRC, select FLEX or STATIC and press YES; assign the desired sample in the normal way.
For scales and glide, open PROJECT > CONTROL > SEQUENCER. Select SCALE, ROOT or GLIDE with UP/DOWN and turn LEVEL. SCALE OFF restores unquantized pitch.

controls.name: PTCH
controls.doc: SRC A: raw 64 is 0 semitones; raw 0–127 gives −64…+63. Scale and chromatic edits can constrain pitch.

controls.name: RATO
controls.doc: SRC B: raw>>2 selects 32 modulation ratios from 0.25 to 16; default raw 12 gives ratio 1.

controls.name: INDX
controls.doc: SRC C: FM modulation depth, raw 0–127. Zero produces the unmodulated carrier.

controls.name: FINE
controls.doc: SRC D: raw 64 is 0 cents; raw 0–127 gives −64…+63 cents.

controls.name: FDBK
controls.doc: SRC E: modulation-operator feedback, raw 0–127. Extreme feedback can be bright and alias.

controls.name: DEC
controls.doc: SRC F: modulation-index decay. Default raw 40 displays about 199 ms. This is separate from the AMP gain envelope.

controls.name: VOIC
controls.doc: LFO C: effective voice count 1–4. Values outside 1–4, including raw 0, normalize to one voice. Initial inherited LFO value displays one; four voices share the track filter and AMP.

controls.name: CHRD
controls.doc: LFO F: 32 chord shapes with four inversions each, encoded as shape<<2 | inversion. ---- uses individual played/recorded notes.

controls.name: LEG
controls.doc: FUNC+AMP F: OFF retriggers, MONO preserves one envelope across overlapping keys, POLY enables paraphonic legato. Ordinary sample tracks expose OFF/MONO.

controls.name: SCALE
controls.doc: OFF restores stock pitch behavior; select a scale to constrain PTCH edits, locks and chromatic keys.

controls.name: ROOT
controls.doc: Root of the scale and chromatic keyboard. Ignored with SCALE OFF.

controls.name: GLIDE
controls.doc: OFF or 1–127 slide time; the track LEG setting controls legato.

limitations: Parts store stock FLEX kind 1 plus FM/1 in unused NEIGHBOR control bytes. A stock build reads the track as FLEX; it does not synthesize FM. Choose stock explicitly before downgrading.
LFO3 speed/depth become VOIC/CHRD; LFO3 depth is muted. ATK/HOLD/REL remain inherited stock AMP controls and drive the synth’s own envelope.
The matching quantizer is bundled privately because the engine shares its mailbox and fixed scale accessor. Do not also select the public Scale Quantizer.

Cannot combine with Analog BD or the public Scale Quantizer because their native hooks overlap. Compatible mixed builds have native/browser byte-parity evidence; mixed audio loads have not been stress-tested.

MIDI selector recovery and one-track mono/four-voice playback are emulator-tested. External MIDI note/CC traffic, saved project/Part reloads, legato, modulation, maximum simultaneous tracks and hardware timing remain unqualified.
Historical upstream marker-FLEX activation remains for compatibility; the verified route is the dedicated FM SYNTH chooser.

Source output is 18.06 dB quieter at identical mixer settings. Added headroom mitigates gain clipping; effects, resonant filtering and summed tracks can still clip. The hardware static report has not been reproduced.

controls.name: REL

controls.name: TYPE
controls.doc: 0–15. Low values favor varied scale notes; higher values prefer tonic/fifth and stronger beat positions. Original algorithm; not a byte-identical Sting port.

controls.name: DENS
controls.doc: 0–16. Note count is round(motif length × DENS / 16). Zero is silence; 16 fills the motif. Changes commit immediately with the current seed.

controls.name: ROOT
controls.doc: C–B. Sample reference is C at neutral PTCH. Tune the source sample accordingly. Pitch locks stay within −12 to +12 semitones.

controls.name: SCAL
controls.doc: Chromatic, natural minor, major, Dorian or minor pentatonic. All generated pitches remain in the selected scale.

controls.name: GATE
controls.doc: 0–126 in native AMP HOLD units, not percent or milliseconds. Generated HOLD locks range from half to all of this value. AMP REL still shapes the audible tail.

controls.name: ACNT
controls.doc: 0–127. Strong notes keep the Part AMP VOL. Other notes are attenuated by up to half; zero gives equal volumes. This writes AMP VOL locks, not MIDI velocity.

controls.name: SEED
controls.doc: 0–127. Select the deterministic variation; YES advances and wraps this value. Other parameter edits keep it fixed.

controls.name: SPAN
controls.doc: 0–12 semitones either side of OFST, clipped to the native ±12-semitone range. Pitches remain in the selected scale; an empty window uses its nearest scale note.

controls.name: OFST
controls.doc: Displayed as −12 to +12 semitones; stored midpoint 12 means zero. Moves the center of the pitch window.

controls.name: ROT
controls.doc: 0–63 steps. Rotate the generated phrase right within the native track length.

controls.name: RPT
controls.doc: OFF (0) uses the full native track length. 1–64 chooses a repeating motif; larger values are clipped to the active length.

controls.name: DIR
controls.doc: FWD or REV. Reverse the generated phrase before applying ROT.

presentation.label: PLAYHEAD DIRECTION
presentation.summary: Play patterns reversed, pingpong, random or shuffled: per pattern, shared by every track or set per track.
presentation.overview: Play Modes changes which step the sequencer plays at each position: NORMAL, REVERSED, PINGPONG (end steps once), PINGPONG 2 (end steps twice), RANDOM or SHUFFLE. Each pattern keeps its own modes: one shared mode under SCALE MODE NORMAL, one per audio and MIDI track under PER TRACK. Trigs, conditions, micro-timing, swing and locks move with their step; tempo, lengths, chains and the trig LEDs stay in step. The modes are saved with the project, survive a power cycle and follow pattern copy, paste and clear.
highlights: Six playhead modes, including two pingpongs and a shuffle that plays every step once per pass
Per pattern; per track under PER TRACK scale mode, audio and MIDI tracks
Hold a TRACK key and press UP or DOWN; a popup names the mode

Each pattern keeps its own modes; PLAY and every pattern change start the tracks from their first step again.
Under PER TRACK, MASTER LENGTH limits how far a track gets; set it to INF to let every track run its full length in every mode.

cpu.rationale: Current 0.2.6 native instruction counts cover eight POLY8 voices, seven FLEX tracks and 24 LFOs. ColdFire owns sample fetching, interpolation and envelopes; measured emulator instructions are not physical utilization or deadlines.

dsp.rationale: POLY8 adds no per-note DSP engine or dynamic loader; its voices share the existing per-track filter and FX path. POLY8 alone preserves both stock DSP uploads; selected DSP mods or Analog BD can modify those payloads.

memory.rationale: Shared 10,586,112-byte reservation once (platform arena plus core logger), reducing sample RAM. Voice state and renderer scratch are fixed allocations; there is no per-note heap allocation.

tests.summary: T07/T08 MKII boot failure was traced to an unloaded initialization flag. Corrected T09 received the owner report "works really well"; the exact T10 selection-flow update then received "works like a charm" on MKII. Duration, separate persistence tests and maximum-load coverage were not reported. Chip deadlines and complete memory bounds remain unqualified under an exact-version owner exception.

tutorial.title: Quick start
steps: Select an audio track, open SRC SETUP, choose POLY8 and press YES.
Only one POLY8 can be assigned in each Part. A second assignment is refused without changing the track; press NO to dismiss the modal. Inactive Parts can each hold one POLY8.

After assignment, POLY8 stays on the current page like FLEX/STATIC. Double-press the track key to open its FLEX sample pool. Load a sample with the stock file browser, then confirm its slot with YES. NO leaves the browser.
Return to SRC, open the trig-mode menu with FUNC+DOWN, select CHROMATIC and confirm with YES. Hold several trig keys; FUNC+LEFT/RIGHT changes octave from -6 to +3.
Turn PTCH to transpose the sounding chord. A dedicated POLY8 MIDI channel accepts notes 0–127; note 84 plays the tuned sample root.
New assignments default to LOOP OFF. POLY8 has a maximum of eight voices, subject to the pitch-work limit, with fixed -18.06 dB gain per voice.
Use REC+PLAY in chromatic mode to record up to four held panel notes spanning at most eleven semitones. Recorded duration follows AMP HOLD.
